author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest brought up a report claiming the 77th Brigade, a British Army unit dedicated to informational operations, was specifically tasked with taking down vaccine misinformation during the pandemic. Russell noted, almost reluctantly, that there was arguably no one in the UK speaking out more against the vaccines, the government, and the media at the time than he was. His guest went further, revealing that academics publicly criticizing lockdown rules had their tweets and activity monitored by the same military unit. Russell called it exactly what it sounds like, the British Army surveilling its own public, and admitted just how disturbing that really is.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest cited studies covering millions of people showing a measurable rise in cancer risk following the Covid vaccination campaign, backed by official government data revealing excess cancer deaths climbing sharply in the aftermath. He argued the pharmaceutical companies behind the shots are deeply intertwined with the oncology industry treating the resulting cancers, creating a financial incentive on both ends. He made the case that scientists invested in a specific outcome don't need to be instructed to lie, the bias happens automatically. Russell pressed on the bigger question hanging over all of it, whether the people and institutions responsible will ever actually be held accountable, given that the same power structures remain firmly in place today.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to what he called one of the most disturbing headlines he's ever seen, involving Charlie Kirk, and admitted he hadn't really looked closely at Dan Bongino's face since he was deputized to the FBI. He noted that Bongino looks visibly worn out now, different somehow. Russell shared a dark, unsettling story a friend once told him about a farm visit involving trays of chicks, some alive, some not, and the strange thing someone did to amuse themselves in that moment. He said that image is exactly what Bongino looks like now, like someone who's simply seen too much. Some weight shows up on a person's face whether they say anything or not.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to a new lab-made butter alternative built from carbon and hydrogen chains rather than animals or plants, funded by Bill Gates, marketed as a breakthrough for sustainable food. He argued this fits a much bigger pattern of replacing agriculture with centrally controlled laboratory food, removing the very things people could once use to resist or opt out entirely. Russell couldn't help but note the irony of celebrating this as good news for everyone, especially for the person behind it, while pointing out who else benefited from proximity to power without facing consequences. Sometimes the strangest part of the future isn't the science, it's who's cheering loudest for it.
